newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Capestar group buys 44 pct of Tej.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Capestar group buys 44 pct of Tej.

text.p: New Western Cape-based investment group, Capestar Growth Investments has bought a 44 percent stake in tightly held Towles, Edgar Jacobs Ltd (Tej), the companies said on Monday.

Tej said it planned to sell its clothing operations as a going concern to subsidiary Enteeb Investments (Proprietary) Ltd, in which CapeStar will hold 60 percent with the balance being held by management.
Tej would then be listed as CapeStar in the investments trusts sector on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, it said.

Tej consists of a consortium of investors led by former Massmart director Michael Rubin, Capital Partners and Fedsure Asset Management which paid eight million rand for 44 percent of Tej's issued ordinary share capital, including 1.1 million previously held by the Jacobs family.

Current preference shares will be converted into ordinary shares, increasing the authorised share capital to 40 million from 5.6 million, increasing tradeability in a stock that dealers say has been little traded.
Minority shareholders will be offered 239 cents a share, but as this is well below the last traded price on June 17 of 300 cents, they are expected to decide to become part of the new group.

A rights offer would be held later in the year to raise 6.2 million rand and the effect of all these transactions would be to leave the new company with about 10 million rand with which to launch a new investment drive in the Western Cape.
"The Western Cape is experiencing superb growth and offers some of the best investment opportunities in the country," Rubin told a media briefing.
CapeStar would target investments of a minimum of two million rand in projects in tourism, agribusiness, the expansion of export led manufacturing, local media and property and financial services.

Rubin said that CapeStar would not take up more than between 20 to 50 percent in any project, none of which would be greenfields projects. No single investment would make up more than 20 percent of total investments.
He expected CapeStar to make between four and six investments over the next 12 months as well as launch another rights offer.
